title: 2026-06-22-calibration-activation-v5.1.0
universal_lens: Isotonic calibration establishes a monotonic, piecewise-constant mapping operator that projects raw heuristic confidence scores onto an empirically observed frequency manifold. This structural transformation enforces the law of large numbers at the boundary layer, ensuring the displayed probability measure aligns exactly with the realized asymptotic hit rate without altering the underlying discriminative ordering.
gsi_mapping: Within GSI, this primitive functions as a conformal post-processing kernel. It adjusts the latent predictive distribution to minimize Expected Calibration Error (ECE), effectively correcting for model overconfidence. The Bayesian posterior is re-weighted via Pool Adjacent Violators Algorithm (PAVA) to guarantee frequentist reliability across all conviction tiers.
gse_mapping: For GSE situational reasoning, isotonic calibration acts as a state-transition gate between internal belief and external action. It ensures that when the engine transitions from silent data collection to public display, the communicated certainty strictly reflects historical empirical outcomes, preventing premature edge manufacturing.

reasoning_traces.think:
The mathematical core of this activation is the decoupling of discriminative power from probabilistic honesty. The base model v5.0.0 produces a raw confidence score $S_{raw}$ derived from fixed heuristic weights. Empirical observation reveals $S_{raw}$ suffers from severe miscalibration, quantified by a raw Expected Calibration Error (ECE) of 0.1980. This indicates the model is systematically overconfident or underconfident across different score intervals. To rectify this without altering the underlying feature engineering, we introduce an isotonic regression operator, specifically utilizing the Pool Adjacent Violators Algorithm (PAVA). This constructs a monotonic, piecewise-constant function $f(S_{raw})$ that maps the raw score to a calibrated probability $P(win)$. The optimization objective is minimizing the squared difference between predicted probabilities and observed frequencies within discrete bins. Crucially, the validation protocol employs a strict 5-fold out-of-fold scheme. By fitting the isotonic map on training folds and evaluating ECE exclusively on held-out data, we prevent in-sample overfitting, a common failure mode in calibration. The resulting calibrated ECE drops to 0.0445, satisfying the activation inequality. Furthermore, the principle of edge invariance dictates that because $f$ is monotonic, the rank ordering of predictions remains identical to v5.0.0. Thus, the Area Under the Curve (AUC) and the raw hit rate (50.9%) remain untouched. The activation merely translates the latent ranking into an honest frequency representation at the user boundary, preparing the system for subsequent edge-generation levers like independent estimator agreement.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This primitive traces its lineage to the foundational work of Niku and Sabes (2004) on isotonic regression for probability calibration, and historically to the Platt scaling methods introduced for SVMs. In quantitative finance and sports intelligence, it represents the critical transition from naive heuristic scoring to rigorous frequentist reliability diagrams, echoing the evolution of weather forecasting models where raw ensemble outputs are routinely adjusted to match historical hit rates before public dissemination.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From the perspective of the decision actor (the founder/engine operator), activating this primitive signals a commitment to epistemic humility. It acknowledges that the current heuristic engine lacks intrinsic predictive edge (trading below the -110 breakeven). By forcing the displayed probabilities to match observed frequencies, the system avoids misleading stakeholders about its true capability. For opposing agents (market makers or bettors), observing these calibrated numbers prevents them from exploiting obvious overconfidence biases, thereby neutralizing a specific class of adversarial extraction strategies until genuine edge is manufactured.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical veto condition exists if the calibration map exhibits extreme volatility or non-monotonicity due to sparse data in certain confidence bins. If the PAVA algorithm collapses distinct confidence tiers into identical calibrated probabilities, the system loses granular situational awareness, effectively flattening the GSE state space. Additionally, if the out-of-fold ECE fails to decrease significantly, it suggests the raw model is not just miscalibrated but fundamentally uninformative (random noise), triggering a hard stop on public display features to prevent reputational damage.
